01 / Version comparison

The same saved viewpoints

Aurum 0.5.7 and 0.5.8 used the same world, camera coordinates, time and 1280 × 720 resolution. Clouds, mobs and animation still move between captures, so this is an image review rather than a pixel-perfect A/B.

Comparison limit: the cloud cover shifts between captures and partly hides the sun in the final water image. This prevents a controlled judgement about glint or sun brightness from these two stills.

04 / Engineering result

What changed, and what still limits it

Implemented in 0.5.8

  • Golden-hour exposure and sky gain leave more room for warm sky colour; the sun disc is larger with a tighter aureole.
  • Reduced diffuse sky fill and stronger leaf interior occlusion improve low-sun voxel separation.
  • Nearby volumetric upscaling uses stronger depth agreement, reducing bright air bleeding across close silhouettes.
  • Water uses smaller, weaker wave layers and calmer far reflections. Ripple, caustic and glitter samples now repeat across 256-block camera rebases.

Remaining visual gap

  • The sky remains a single-scattering LUT; distant air and cloud lighting lack the richer multi-scattering response of the references.
  • Open-ocean glitter is present, but its density and variety still trail Photon, and water lacks a complete reflection environment.
  • Sky, terrain and water are tone-mapped in separate display paths into an 8-bit scene. This limits highlight and colour cohesion.
  • Rays and foliage need moving-camera review at native 1080p, especially near tree edges.
